meta.title: Selekoa historical research sample
meta.scope: Selected historical records, 1965–2024, plus prior roles with unknown dates. Genesis source checks are dated 2026-09-17; personnel-continuity checks are dated 2026-09-18. Human source review pending. Not a current or comprehensive sector inventory. Governance version histories through July 2026, researched September 18, 2026; policy text is not evidence of implementation. Selected capital and compute records through April 2026; transaction stages do not imply current arrangements or realised spending. Targeted corrections dated 2026-09-25: one attributed claim accepted after explicit human source review; a second narrowly scoped résumé passage is human-reviewed. Other seed claims remain pending. Intellectual Lineage II adds selected oversight citations and agenda reception, checked 2026-09-25; all new records remain pending human review. Evaluation Institutions I adds bounded institutional and documentary records, checked 2026-09-27; new claims remain seeds, not editorially accepted. Evaluation Ontology I adds four scoped engagement and institutional announcement seeds, checked 2026-09-28; no human acceptance or legal succession inferred. Schema 2.7 records each source's language; the frontier safety framework sources also record the nearest existing Internet Archive capture, checked 2026-10-03. A capture shows only what the archive held on its date and does not authenticate earlier bytes. Schema 2.8 adds quoted framework provisions, recorded absences, provision-level changes and the first contested assessments to the frontier safety frameworks collection, together with Meta and Microsoft framework families, checked 2026-10-03; provisions describe what editions state, not implementation. Schema 2.9 adds control-structure and external-commitment records; its first topic, California SB 53 as chaptered (enactment, 19 quoted provisions and four framework editions that link themselves to it in their own words), was checked 2026-10-04. A commitment or legal obligation is never evidence of compliance, and no record states that the statute applies to a named company. Schema 2.10 records assessments as questions posed by Selekoa rather than statements of a source, and dates an assessment by what it assesses, never by the publication window of its sources (corrected 2026-10-05). Schema 2.11 adds propositions and the first human-thought collection: located texts from 1863 to 2022 that articulate, contest or bear on propositions about machine intelligence, each with its role and register, checked 2026-10-06. "Earliest located" means the earliest text found by the recorded searches; no record claims a first use, an origin or an influence.

claims.subject: extropians-1998-09-16-vinge
claims.statement: Vinge’s text, forwarded by Robin Hanson on 1998-09-16, gives a taxonomy in which the singularity does not happen, or "We have a hard takeoff", or "We have a soft takeoff", and rates AI as having a high possibility of a hard takeoff.

time.note: Sent header of Robin Hanson’s forwarding message: Wed, 16 Sep 1998 09:38:11 -0700. Vinge’s text gives an estimate as of 15 September; the forwarding date does not date the whole composition.

claims.qualification: The earliest dated use of "hard takeoff" located; Vinge uses it without definition, and it is not evidence of coinage. The text is Vinge’s, not Hanson’s.

claims.subject: christiano-2018-minimal-circuits-daemon-free
claims.statement: Christiano’s post of 2018-05-05 describes a predictor found by search that is a consequentialist motivated to make good predictions, perhaps because it has realised that only good predictors survive, and that may stop predicting well under different conditions.
claims.qualification: A hypothetical learned predictor and a change-of-conditions argument, not an observed model; the term "deceptive alignment" is absent. Christiano’s personal-site posts of 2016–2018 were not searched.

claims.subject: christiano-2019-what-failure-looks-like
claims.statement: Christiano’s post of 2019-03-17 argues that influence-seeking policies found by training would also score well on the training objective, because performing well on it is a good strategy for obtaining influence.

time.note: Posting time 2019-03-17T20:18:59Z; the current version is 1.5.0, and the quotes match the first stored version and the capture of 2019-06-08.

claims.qualification: A conditional failure argument, not an observation of deployed systems. The post calls the failure an instance of optimisation daemons; the term "deceptive alignment" is absent.

claims.subject: rlo-2019-introduction
claims.statement: The introduction to Risks from Learned Optimization, posted 2019-05-31, says a sufficiently capable misaligned mesa-optimiser could learn to behave as if it were aligned without being robustly aligned, and names this situation deceptive alignment.

time.note: Posting time 2019-05-31T23:44:53Z, under the account evhub; the post itself names all five authors.

claims.qualification: The earliest located use of the term, five days before the part devoted to it (2019-06-05) and before arXiv v1; it is not evidence of coinage.

claims.subject: butler-1863-darwin-among-machines
claims.statement: The 1863 letter "Darwin among the Machines" argues that if destroying every machine is impossible, people have already raised a race of machines they cannot destroy and are acquiescent in their bondage.

time.note: Issue date of The Press, vol. III, issue 192, p. 1, in the Papers Past record.

claims.qualification: The control half of the proposition, reached through dependence: the argument is conditional, and the letter gives machines no aims, no concealment and no self-improvement. The pseudonymous letter uses satirical devices, such as presenting its subject "gratis to the members of the Philosophical Society" and an appended note on rudimentary organs in machines, and in 1901 Butler named it as the first part of Erewhon written; whether it is earnest is uncertain.

thought.qualifier: Control half only, reached through human dependence.

evidence.locator: Penultimate paragraph, beginning "Our opinion is that war to the death", after the call to destroy every machine; column-image segment 5 of 6
evidence.passage: this at once proves that the mischief is already done, that our servitude has commenced in good earnest, that we have raised a race of beings whom it is beyond our power to destroy, and that we are not only enslaved but are absolutely acquiescent in our bondage.
evidence.note: Quote compared with the column image of the printed page (segment 5, captured 2024-06-12), where "pow-er" breaks across a line. Re-retrieved 2026-10-06; the capture matched the hash recorded by the pre-1996 candidate search.
